attacks.claim: The rollout reports beta results (0 lost saves, 11 conflict prompts) from a Nov 18-30 beta, but today is 2026-10-26, so that evidence cannot exist yet. The gate relies on uncollected data.
attacks.evidence: "1. Nov 18-30: public opt-in beta branch ... 0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts, all resolved by players."

attacks.claim: QA ran on a private Steam branch and an Epic dev-sandbox build, yet the summary calls it the release build. Results may not carry over to the shipping binaries, and the Epic path (29% of players) is unvalidated on a production build.
attacks.evidence: "QA ran on the release build 1.4.0 (Steam build 18204411 on a private branch, Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox)"

attacks.claim: The conflict rule depends on a 'since last sync' baseline. On first link, or after reinstall, with existing local and cloud saves, the artifact does not say whether the game prompts or silently applies the newer copy. This bears directly on the no-lost-saves requirement.
attacks.evidence: "If both changed since last sync, the game asks" (ABSENT: behavior on first link or reinstall with no baseline)

attacks.claim: Unlink-and-delete permanently removes all server copies and version history, including progress from the other store's device that may not yet be on this PC. No warning, confirmation, or unsynced-progress check is specified, and there is no grace period.
attacks.evidence: "removes the link and all server copies within 24 h (local saves untouched)" (ABSENT: confirmation, unsynced-progress warning, retention window)

attacks.claim: Unlink-and-delete is irreversible, but the artifact does not require fresh re-authentication from both stores. A single valid or stolen session, or a shared PC, could destroy cloud saves, and the 24 h delay gives no immediate revocation.
attacks.evidence: "Settings > Cross-Save > 'Unlink and delete cloud saves' removes the link and all server copies within 24 h"

attacks.claim: Epic under-13 (cabined) restriction is enforced only by hiding the UI. Nothing says the server rejects link creation for cabined accounts, and QA checked only that the screen is hidden. A modified client or direct API call could link them.
attacks.evidence: "for them linking is not offered and the screen explains why." QA: "Linking not offered, explanation shown"

attacks.claim: Client-supplied last-modified in sync.meta drives the automatic cloud download. The artifact does not say server-side timestamps are authoritative, so a forged or future-dated value could replace the local save without a prompt.
attacks.evidence: "On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older." and "`sync.meta` sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)"

attacks.claim: Multi-slot blob uploads and the sidecar upload are not described as atomic. A partial success can leave server metadata (timestamps, playtime) disagreeing with the saves, which breaks the conflict prompt.
attacks.evidence: "Sync uploads the existing save slots plus a small `sync.meta` sidecar" (ABSENT: commit protocol and partial-upload recovery)

attacks.claim: Downloads and restores overwrite local saves, but the artifact does not say the write is atomic (temp file, fsync, rename). A crash or power loss mid-write could corrupt the only local copy, undermining the no-lost-saves guarantee.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: temp-file-then-rename or fsync handling for writes to saves/ and saves/backup/. Only checksum verification before load is described.

attacks.claim: Installed 1.4 clients are not downgraded by restoring 1.3 as the default branch. The artifact does not describe how they return to 1.3 or what happens to their synced state. Only a Steam downgrade was tested, with no Epic downgrade test.
attacks.evidence: "1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores"; QA: "Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`)"

attacks.claim: The server accepts blobs unparsed and keeps only 5 versions per slot, with up to 60 uploads per hour. A client that repeatedly writes bad but checksum-valid saves could push out the last good server copy within minutes, and the 3 local backups add little margin.
attacks.evidence: "the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally" alongside "60 uploads per hour per player."

attacks.claim: The game is required never to block on the network, but the launch-time conflict prompt needs cloud metadata, and no timeouts are given for that fetch, token minting, or Steam/EOS validation. A slow backend could stall the title screen.
attacks.evidence: "The game never blocks on the network" (ABSENT: timeout values for launch-time metadata fetch, conflict decision, token exchange)

attacks.claim: The data claim says no name data is stored, but sync.meta uploads a free-text device name that players often set to their real name, and the server stores it. The stated data inventory is contradicted by the actual fields.
attacks.evidence: "No email, name, payment or friends data." vs "`sync.meta` sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)"

attacks.claim: Retention for the steam_id↔epic_account_id link is undefined. The 24-month inactivity rule covers only cloud save data, so the cross-platform identity linkage could persist indefinitely.
attacks.evidence: "Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted" (no statement on link retention); link stored as "steam_id ↔ epic_account_id"

attacks.claim: The deletion promise covers only the link and server copies. Backups, replicas, logs and analytics holding Steam/Epic IDs, device names or playtime are not addressed, so the deletion claim may be incomplete.
attacks.evidence: "removes the link and all server copies within 24 h"; no mention of backups, logs or replicas

attacks.claim: Alerts do not cover failures of the 24-hour deletion job or the 24-month retention job, even though both carry stated privacy promises. Alerts also omit Steam/EOS validation failures and checksum rejections.
attacks.evidence: "Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate."

attacks.claim: The restore-spike threshold is tied to the 2,300 + 150 beta population. That baseline may not match restore rates across the full player base, so the alert may fire constantly or never.
attacks.evidence: "any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate"

attacks.claim: The kill switch is read from the backend it is meant to protect, and the client default when the config is unreachable is not stated. The budget auto-flip is also not specified, and server copies keep accruing storage cost after sync is off.
attacks.evidence: "Kill switch `cross_save_enabled=false` (server config, read on launch and every 10 min)"; "at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically"

attacks.claim: No backoff or retry schedule is specified. Retries could exhaust the 60/hour upload quota, and the client behavior when rate-limited is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "60 uploads per hour per player." (ABSENT: retry schedule, backoff, rate-limited handling)

attacks.claim: Epic cabined restriction is handled, but Steam accounts have no age handling, and the artifact does not address minors linking and sending identifiers and behavioral metadata to the EU backend.
attacks.evidence: "Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered" (no equivalent for Steam)

attacks.claim: Request logs, 5xx traces and dashboards will likely carry IPs and account IDs, but no log content or retention rules are set.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: log fields, IP handling, retention. "Dashboard: link success rate, sync errors by type, conflict prompts, restore usage..."

attacks.claim: The checksum is not a keyed MAC and gives no tamper protection. Client-side v3 schema validation is the only defense for crafted blobs, and no parser fuzzing or hardening is mentioned. Device name is also not length-limited or sanitized before display in the conflict prompt.
attacks.evidence: "The client verifies the save's checksum and v3 schema before loading"; "device name" shown in "Keep the save on this PC (...)"

attacks.claim: Rate limits exist only for save uploads. Link creation, token minting and session validation have no stated limits, which leaves room for abuse of the store-validation path and cost inflation.
attacks.evidence: "60 uploads per hour per player." (no limit for linking or token minting)

attacks.claim: The one-link-per-store-account rule is not shown to be enforced atomically. Concurrent link requests could race past the uniqueness check.
attacks.evidence: "Each store account can be in at most one link."

attacks.claim: Storage, rotation and scoping of backend Steam and EOS credentials are not described, although session validation depends on them.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: storage, rotation, scoping of Steam Web API key and EOS client secret

attacks.claim: The hard $600 budget stop depends on an automation that flips the kill switch, but the mechanism and its tested behavior are not named. Billing alerts usually only notify, so the cost ceiling may not exist.
attacks.evidence: "hard project budget stop at $600/month; at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically."
